citations.A1: Cache has no invalidation — it's keyed on nothing and never checked against the file, so store the file's mtime (and size) alongside the data and reload when it differs.
citations.A2: adding a time-based TTL (still serves stale data for the window and re-reads when nothing changed — it masks the missing invalidation rather than fixing it)
citations.A3: calling `get_config.cache_clear()`-style tricks or switching to `functools.lru_cache` (same never-invalidated cache, now keyed by path — it fixes finding 3 only)
citations.A4: `path` is ignored after the first call — a second call with a different path silently returns the first file's data, so key the cache by resolved absolute path in a dict.
citations.A5: Not thread-safe — two threads can both see `None` and race on the parse, so guard load-and-store with a lock (double-checked).
citations.A8: `_cache is None` conflates "not loaded" with "loaded and empty/null" — a config file containing `null` reloads every call; use a distinct sentinel or a separate `_loaded` flag.
